prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity landscape desktop website first-viewport comp for a public developer portfolio homepage
Primary request: Create exactly one polished 1536×1024 desktop homepage composition for the confirmed visual identity “ANALYST’S WORKING PAPER,” variation “EVIDENCE WORKBENCH.” The visual lineage is an equity-research tear sheet fused with a developer inspection bench. It must unmistakably look like a usable responsive public portfolio website, not a poster, slide, magazine cover, or atmosphere image.

Scene/backdrop: Full-bleed straight-on desktop webpage canvas, no browser chrome, no device mockup, no perspective distortion. Pale paper background #F4F7F5.

Subject: Marc Mansour, a developer focused on financial tools who builds and writes about technology, development, and finance. The hero is organized as one oversized product workbench: a compact left-aligned thesis band across the top of the content area, followed by a near-full-width, highly inspectable schematic finance-app specimen. The specimen is an unnamed personal-finance application interface with a cash-flow chart, spending allocation, account rows, and code/model fragments, shown only as schematic UI with no readable invented numbers. Surround the specimen with carbon-pencil margin notes, proof marks, registration crosses, snippets of formula notation, thin cobalt arrows, and a few signal-red editorial circles. Attach a narrow pinned evidence slip labeled “Recent public activity” to the right edge of the specimen, with a small GitHub-style activity grid and the handle “marcm8793”; do not show any contribution totals. The next fold should begin at the bottom with a rigorous project index and journal/blog ledger.

Style/medium: High-fidelity editorial web UI, rigorous information design, analyst notebook meets software portfolio, warm human annotations over precise grid systems. Flat front-on interface design. Refined typography, strong hierarchy, generous negative space, production-realistic interaction affordances, crisp 1px rules. Avoid generic fintech aesthetics.

Composition/framing: 1536×1024 landscape. Compact top header. Navigation items look like workbook index tabs. Hero begins with a slim numbered eyebrow “01 / FINANCE × SOFTWARE”, a strong serif headline on the left and supporting text plus two actions aligned beneath. The dominant app specimen spans roughly 70% of page width and 55% of the viewport height, with annotations extending into quiet gutters. The GitHub activity slip is pinned onto its right side, secondary but clearly readable. Reveal about 20% of the second section at the bottom. Keep all content safely within the canvas.

Lighting/mood: Bright diffuse paper-like daylight, cerebral, credible, exploratory, precise, not glossy.

Color palette: paper #F4F7F5, ink #101828, cobalt #174EA6, data lime #B6F23A, signal red #D93D45. Cobalt rules and annotations; lime used sparingly for activity/data marks; red only for proof marks.

Materials/textures: subtle recycled paper grain, blue ledger ruling, carbon annotations, translucent chart overlays, index tabs, pinned data slips, registration marks; retain clean modern web UI legibility.

Text (verbatim, render every item exactly and legibly):
Brand: “MARC MANSOUR”
Navigation: “HOME”, “PROJECTS”, “ABOUT”, “RESUME”, “CONTACT”, “BLOG”
Eyebrow: “01 / FINANCE × SOFTWARE”
Headline: “Developer focused on financial tools.”
Supporting line: “I build and write about technology, development, and finance.”
Primary action: “Explore my work”
Secondary action: “Read the journal”
Product label: “FINANCIAL APP / WORKING MODEL”
GitHub label: “Recent public activity”
GitHub handle: “marcm8793”
Next-section labels: “SELECTED WORK” and “FIELD NOTES”

Constraints: Exact visible copy only as specified above; nav must clearly read as navigation; both actions must clearly read as actionable controls; show clear webpage structure and usable alignment; the financial app specimen must remain unnamed and schematic; no profile portrait; no logos; no stock photography; no readable invented numbers, metrics, company names, clients, testimonials, awards, employers, or claims. Preserve spelling, capitalization, and punctuation of all required text.

Avoid: generic fintech dashboard, bento grid, centered hero, polished corporate deck, glowing gradients, dark crypto UI, banking app cliché, fake analytics, invented charts with readable values, invented metrics, dates, company names, clients, testimonials, app names, employers, awards, fake article titles, fake body copy, poster composition, browser chrome, watermark, illegible or misspelled required text.
